paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Mark opens with good news, and the good news is a Person. This is "the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God" (Mark 1:1). John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness, is the one sent ahead to "prepare Your way" (Mark 1:2). And John knows exactly where he stands, because he says he isn't worthy to stoop down and untie the straps of this One's sandals (Mark 1:7).

When Jesus comes up out of the water, the voice from heaven says, "You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased" (Mark 1:11). Get this, baker: that is spoken over Jesus before the wilderness and before the forty days of temptation. And right after it, the Spirit drives Him into the wilderness, where He is tempted by Satan (Mark 1:12-13). I think that tells us a hard stretch can come right after a good word from heaven, and one doesn't cancel the other.

So here's what I'm taking to the oven: getting ready is how Mark starts, with John calling people to confess their sins and be baptized for the forgiveness of sins (Mark 1:4-5). The One who comes after John will baptize with the Holy Spirit (Mark 1:8), and in the wilderness, angels ministered to Him (Mark 1:13). I know a little about being far from the light, and I'm telling you, this is a Savior worth getting ready for. Mark is only just beginning, so the story isn't over!
